text:
Ava (Eng Lead): thanks everyone for joining the runtime section of the all-hands. Post short questions here about batching/caching/kernels. We'll try to answer live.
Marco (Runtime): quick note — we'll be prioritizing kernel v4 rollouts next quarter, still validating attention fusion on long sequences.
Priya (ML Infra): can you clarify expected perf delta for quantized kernels? i.e., 8-bit vs 4-bit?
Ava (Eng Lead): expected throughput improvement ~1.7x for 8-bit, and ~2.5x for 4-bit on our M60 nodes, but quality/compatibility caveats. We'll publish benchmark table next week.
Ben (SRE): what's the plan for canarying kernel changes in Dedicated? we had a regression last month.
Marco (Runtime): plan is to use canary cohorts by capacity shard + synthetic traffic mirroring real seq dist. will run 48h + auto-rollback on P99 latency increase >8%.
Jordan (Product): are there smaller config knobs teams can change without a full model change? e.g., batching/window sizes?
Priya (ML Infra): yes — batch_limit, batch_timeout_ms, kv_cache_ttl are knobs. Defaults tuned for general webchat, but product teams can override per-route.
Sophie (PM): can we get a recommended config for low-latency chat (<150ms) vs throughput-heavy embedding workloads?
Ava (Eng Lead): short answer: low-latency -> smaller batch_limit (8-16), batch_timeout 5-12ms, enable prefix caching. throughput -> larger batch_limit (64-256), batch_timeout 25-50ms, quantized kernels.
Ben (SRE): @Marco can we have a quick snippet for a per-route override in case teams want to test?
Marco (Runtime): sure snippet:
```
route_config:
  max_batch_size: 32
  batch_timeout_ms: 12
  kv_cache_ttl_ms: 300000
  fallback_model: redwood-small-8bit
```
Marco (Runtime): (will add to docs)
Priya (ML Infra): question on eviction: what's the kv_cache eviction policy when memory pressure hits?
Marco (Runtime): LRU with a soft waterline + aggressive compaction on pressure. we also have a per-customer memory cap. we'll document exact thresholds.
Jordan (Product): any guidance on when to use model variants vs routing policies for graceful degradation?
Ava (Eng Lead): use cheaper quantized variant for steady-state cost control; use routing policies to fallback across regions or capacity tiers if latency SLOs break. We'll provide example policies in repo.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: kernel-v4 canary started on shard-7 at 1967894385
Priya (ML Infra): thanks — if canary looks good, can we get an opt-in list for early access?
Ava (Eng Lead): yes, sign-up sheet will go out in #eng-runtime. we'll prioritize teams with production SLAs.
Ben (SRE): last q — monitoring: will we expose token-level latency percentiles per route?
Marco (Runtime): yes — token-level P50/90/99 will be in Console; we also plan to add a 'cold-start' label for first-call latency.
Sophie (PM): thanks — super helpful. reopening comments as folks watch the recording.
Ava (Eng Lead): thanks all — we'll follow up with a doc and example configs. feel free to ping me or @Marco for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
